main_text.p: riæ eius sunt differentiæ, propterea uaria à nobis proponenda erunt remedia. Idcircò quæ à sanguine crasso & melancholico orta est, copiosiore, & frequentiore sanguinis missione indiget, quàm quæ ab adusta bile nascitur: & hæc adhuc, magis quá reliquæ, quę quidem catharticis phlegmagogis, potius profligari postulant. Igitur Galenus commentario in Aphorismum quadragesimum septimum, Sectionis septimę nō de postremarum curatione uerba fecit, sed de his, quæ à fece sanguinis, & bile torrefacta originem duxêre, dū incipientem elephantiasim se sanasse ait, primo quidem uenæ sectione & purgatione: dein uerò singulis annis pharmacum melanagogum propinans. De ijsdem loquuntur Cornelius Celsus, Paulus Ægineta, & Aëtius, qui non solùm melanagogum præscribunt, sed & phlebotomiam sæpe repetitam. Propterea dū Cornelius protinus inter initia sanguinem esse mittendum per biduum præcipit, cum de sanguinea elephantia loquitur: cùm uerò ueratro nigro uentrem esse soluendum ait, cum etiam biliosam intelligit, quæ potius catharticum, quàm phlebotomiam postulat, propterea quòd in hac genuini sanguinis

page.notes: The text is set in a long-s typeface where s looks like f; all such letters are transcribed as s. Line-end words without a printed hyphen (e.g. "po|stulat", "quadrage-simum" with its hyphen kept) are written whole or with the printed hyphen. The catchword is printed only as "guinis" at the right; the rest of the word lies on the line above, so only the visible part is given. The printed "melanagogum" in the second sentence is transcribed as printed. No headings, no notes in the margins.
